newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in London, Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in London, Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Leading shares settled lower, tracking steep losses on Wall Street as signs of economic growth in the United States heightened expectations that the Federal Reserve will tighten credit later this month. The benchmark FTSE 100 share index closed 24.8 points lower at 4,397.7.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended bourse trade down nearly 2 percent, catching up with losses in IBIS trade from Wednesday and fresh pressure from a weaker dollar and overnight Wall Street losses. The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 65.59 points at 3,349.81 points but off the day's low at 3,338.53 points. In post-bourse trade the Dax stood at 3,367.82.

PARIS - Shares clambered back off the day's lows but closed slightly softer. A bigger-than-expected rise in U.S. February retail sales of 0.8 percent sent bond and stock prices lower, but the CAC index narrowed the loss as a few blue-chip rises gave support. The CAC-40 index closed down 9.60 points or 0.36 percent at 2,632.10.

ZURICH - Shares closed more than 1 percent lower, but shares of Ciba Speciality Chemicals saw solid demand on their first day of trading. Dealers said the easing U.S. dollar, a fall on U.S. and European bourses, as well as weakness in bonds, contributed to the market's slide. The all-share SPI fell 31.75 points to 2,922.70.

TOKYO - The stock market's key Nikkei 225 index ended at its lowest level since Feb. 7 as sentiment weakened on a series of corporate scandals. The Nikkei average of 225 shares shed 282.79 points, or 1.56 percent, to end at 17,900.48.

HONG KONG - A selloff in the property sector sent stocks tumbling through support to end sharply lower as investors feared the government may intervene to curb escalating prices in the property market. The Hang Seng Index slid 202.04 points to 12,917.09, ending below psychological support at 13,000 points.
SYDNEY - A slow share market ended barely changed as the market drifted with little motivation or interest from traders. The All Ordinaries index lost 1.8 points to 2,452.6.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks ended up but sharply off their day highs as the market. The gold index shed 17.9 points to 1,429.6. The all-share index ended up 3.7 points at 7,171.6, and industrials gained 5.5 points to 8,373.7.
